title: SIP step-up compliance
objectives: State the do's and don'ts for recommending a step-up.
Check an illustration for the two things that must always appear.
body_md:
Every step-up conversation ends with the same compliance frame.

## Do

- Check the emergency fund, loans and budget before suggesting a step-up.
- Show projections as illustrative, with the assumed return and the higher total invested.
- Explain the AMC's top-up terms, cap and mandate limit.
- Mention that converting a SIP may mean re-registration and new exit-load terms.
- Record the agreed step-up rule and review date.

## Don't

- Push a step-up the client can't sustain.
- Show only the final corpus without the extra money invested.
- Promise that a step-up will reach a goal.
- Cancel and re-register a SIP without explaining the effects.
- Raise a step-up without the client's documented consent.

## The two things every illustration needs

The assumed return, labelled illustrative, and the total invested. A number without either is a promise in disguise.
example: "A 10% step-up will get you ₹2 crore" becomes "Illustratively, at 12% assumed, a 10% step-up invests about ₹68.7 L and could reach about ₹2 crore; not guaranteed."
say: Illustratively, at 12% assumed, this step-up invests about ₹68.7 lakh and could reach about ₹2 crore.
Converting this SIP means re-registering it, which restarts the exit-load clock on new units.
never: The step-up will get you to ₹2 crore.
Just re-register the SIP; nothing changes.

talk_track.title: Compliance: what we say, and what we never say
talk_track.text: Do check the client's emergency fund, loans and budget before suggesting a step-up. Do show the extra money invested, not just the final result. Do explain the fund house's terms, the cap and the mandate limit. Do explain any re-registration and exit-load effects. And do record the agreed step-up rule and the review date. Don't push a step-up the client can't sustain. Don't show only the final corpus. Don't promise that a step-up will reach a goal.
